query: What does Section 20 say about children under seven years?

gold_references.label: Section 20
gold_references.role: act of a child under seven years of age - no offence

acceptable_references.label: Section 21
acceptable_references.reason: closely related provision for children between 7 and 12

required_points: Section 20 provides that nothing is an offence which is done by a child under seven years of age.
A child below seven years has complete immunity from criminal liability under BNS.
optional_points: Section 21 provides a qualified exception for children above seven and under twelve years of age who have not attained sufficient maturity of understanding.
forbidden_points: A child under seven can be punished if the act is serious.
Section 20 sets the age of criminal responsibility at twelve.

notes: Direct lookup. Section 20 is the absolute criminal immunity provision for children under 7.
